cards.text: It's the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia. A message is revealed to Daniel, who was also called Belteshazzar, and the message is true. The understanding of it comes to him in a vision.

cards.question: This true message is revealed to Daniel in the third year of Cyrus. What is it about?

cards.text: Now Daniel picks up the story himself: "In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks." Not three days, friend. THREE. FULL. WEEKS.

cards.question: During his three full weeks of mourning, Daniel keeps eating rich food the same as always.

cards.text: No rich food, no meat or wine, and he doesn't anoint himself with oil until the three weeks are done. Then, on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, Daniel's standing on the bank of a great river.

cards.question: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, which great river is Daniel standing beside?

cards.text: Daniel lifts up his eyes, and behold. A certain man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist.

cards.question: The man in linen that Daniel sees by the river looks just like any ordinary man.

cards.text: "His body was like beryl, his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of polished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude." Friend, back in the junk drawer I used to squint when somebody opened it to the kitchen light. This man's FACE is like lightning.
Here's the thing. Only Daniel sees the vision, and the men with him don't see a thing, but a great terror falls on them anyway.

cards.question: The men with Daniel don't see the vision, but a great terror falls on them. What do they do?

answers.text: They call out to the man

cards.text: They ran and hid from a vision they didn't even SEE. That's me hearing one creak in a dark kitchen at night. Saw nothing. Hid anyway.

cards.question: Left alone gazing at this great vision, Daniel feels his strength come rushing back.

cards.text: Not even close. No strength remains in him, his face grows deathly pale, and then he hears the sound of the man's words.

cards.question: As Daniel listens to the sound of the man's words, what happens to him?

answers.text: He falls into a deep sleep
He runs off to find his men
He walks out into the river

cards.text: Face to the ground, and suddenly a hand touches him and sets him trembling on his hands and knees. Then he hears, "Daniel, you are a man who is highly precious."

cards.question: The voice tells Daniel to consider carefully the words to come, and to stand up. What reason does it give for standing up?

answers.text: He has now been sent to Daniel
The three weeks are not over

cards.question: Once he's told to stand, Daniel stays down on his hands and knees.

cards.text: "Do not be afraid, Daniel," he says. Daniel set out to understand and to humble himself before his God, and his words were heard.

cards.question: Daniel set out to understand and to humble himself before his God. When were his words heard?

answers.text: On the last day of mourning

cards.text: From day ONE, and he says he's come in response to those words. But Daniel's been mourning three full weeks, so what took so long?

cards.question: Daniel's words were heard on day one, but the one sent to him arrives after three weeks. What opposed him?

answers.text: The prince of the kingdom of Persia
A flood on the great river Tigris
The armies of the king of Egypt

cards.text: Opposed for twenty-one days. Do the math, friend: that's three full weeks, the same stretch Daniel spent mourning, and I start pacing when the oven timer says three MINUTES.

cards.question: During those twenty-one days of opposition, someone comes to help the one sent to Daniel. Who?

cards.text: Michael, one of the chief princes, comes to help, for the one speaking had been left there with the kings of Persia.

cards.question: He's finally made it to Daniel. What has he come to explain?

answers.text: What will happen to Daniel's people in the latter days
Why Daniel's men ran away and hid by the river
How Daniel should bring his three weeks of mourning to an end

cards.text: While he's speaking, Daniel sets his face toward the ground and becomes speechless. Then one with the likeness of a man touches Daniel's lips.

cards.question: Once his lips are touched, Daniel opens his mouth and speaks.
Daniel says he's overcome with anguish, with no strength and no breath left in him. What does the one with the likeness of a man do?

answers.text: He touches Daniel again and strengthens him
He tells Daniel to rest until morning
He sends Daniel back to find his men

cards.text: "Do not be afraid, you who are highly precious," he says. "Peace be with you! Be strong now; be very strong!"

cards.question: After hearing "be very strong," Daniel asks him to hold off speaking for now.

cards.text: Daniel's strengthened, and he says, "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me." So he asks Daniel, "Do you know why I have come to you?"

cards.question: The one speaking with Daniel says he must return at once. What for?

answers.text: To fight against the prince of Persia
To bring back the men who hid
To guard the bank of the Tigris

cards.text: And once he's gone forth, behold, the prince of Greece will come. But first, he'll tell Daniel what is inscribed in the Book of Truth.

cards.question: Against these, he says no one has the courage to support him except ___, Daniel's prince.

cards.text: Then he says, "And I, in the first year of Darius the Mede, stood up to strengthen and protect him." The Book of Truth is about to open, friend, so stay close, because this story's not done.

findings.problem: Daniel is named without being introduced. Cyrus gets 'king of Persia', but Daniel gets no simple line saying who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: the full Daniel 10:6 quote, 'Friend, back in the junk drawer I used to squint…', and 'This man's FACE is like lightning.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card only restates the answer to card 11 ('They ran and hid from a vision they didn't even SEE') and adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage, so it doesn't move the baker forward.
The joke invents a new backstory moment in which Papa Dorin hears a creak in a dark kitchen and hides. His backstory has him on the counter or in the drawer, and this adds to it.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'They ran and hid…', 'That's me hearing…', 'Saw nothing.' and 'Hid anyway.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Face to the ground', which comes from Daniel 10:9, but it cites only Daniel 10:10-11. It should cite Daniel 10:9-11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The choice cards almost strictly alternate types: MC, TF, MC, TF, MC, TF, MC, MC, TF. The order reads as a pattern.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'A flood on the great river Tigris' is a natural event. The right answer and the other wrong answer are powers or rulers, so the flood isn't the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The question says Michael comes to help 'During those twenty-one days'. Daniel 10:13 says the prince of Persia opposed him for twenty-one days, and 'Then Michael… came to help me.' The text does not place Michael's help inside the twenty-one days.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'He's finally made it to Daniel.' 'He' points back to cards the baker can no longer see, and the question never says who he is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question has Daniel ask 'him' to hold off speaking, and it never says who 'him' is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Against these' and 'he says… support him' point back to card 16 (the princes of Persia and Greece) and to an unnamed speaker. The question doesn't say who or what these are.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Darius the Mede shows up for the first time in the quote, and the card never says simply who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain retellings or bare quotes with no Papa Dorin voice. Examples are stop 1 cards 7 and 10, and stop 2 cards 1, 7, 9, 12, 14 and 16. Stop 2 has only one joke across nine story cards, and the walkthrough rarely reaches laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend.
